title: Confidence Calibration in Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: arXiv:2507.17383v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Trustworthy robot behavior requires not only high levels of task success but also that the robot can reliably quantify how likely it is to succeed. To this end, we present a first-of-its-kind study of confidence calibration in vision-language-action (VLA) foundation models, which map visual observations and natural language instructions to low-level robot motor commands. We establish a confidence estimation baseline for VLAs, examine how task success relates to calibration error and how calibration evolves over time, and introduce two lightweight techniques to remedy the miscalibration we observe: prompt ensembles and action-wise Platt scaling. Our aim in this study is to begin to develop the tools and conceptual understanding necessary to render VLAs trustworthy via reliable uncertainty quantification.

translated_title: 视觉-语言-动作模型的置信度校准
translated_abstract: 可信赖的机器人行为不仅需要高水平的任务成功率，还需要机器人能够可靠地量化其成功的可能性。为此，我们首次对视觉-语言-动作（VLA）基础模型中的置信度校准进行了系统性研究，该类模型将视觉观察和自然语言指令映射到底层机器人运动指令。我们为VLA建立了置信度估计基线，考察了任务成功与校准误差之间的关系以及校准随时间的演变规律，并提出了两种轻量级技术来纠正我们所观察到的校准偏差：提示集成和动作级Platt缩放。本研究的目的是开始开发必要的工具和概念理解，以便通过可靠的不确定性量化使VLA模型变得可信赖。
tldr: 本文首次系统研究了视觉-语言-动作（VLA）基础模型的置信度校准问题，建立了置信度估计基线，并提出提示集成与动作级Platt缩放两种轻量级技术来改善校准，从而通过可靠的不确定性量化提升机器人行为的可信赖性。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first-of-its-kind study of confidence calibration in vision-language-action (VLA) foundation models, establishing a confidence estimation baseline and introducing two lightweight techniques—prompt ensembles and action-wise Platt scaling—to remedy miscalibration and enable trustworthy robot behavior through reliable uncertainty quantification.
